```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

necessary libraries
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(readr)
library(openxlsx)
```

load in gis city geocoded data from our arcGIS map. exported straight from our map. Our objective is to get every unique city / state combo and make a csv with it so the searching process is straightforward
```{r}
gismaster = read.csv("master_spreadsheet_by_individual_award__GIS_version__07302026_CITY_Geocoded_3.csv", header = TRUE)
```

subset to only the features we care about
```{r}
gismaster2 = gismaster[, c("Match.Address", "X", "Y")]
```


We then get rid of any duplicated entries in city state. as this spreadsheet will be used as a map layer to make searching a seemless experience, this makes sense
```{r}
gismaster3 = gismaster2[!duplicated(gismaster2$Match.Address), ]
```

We also omit NAs so mapping is easier
```{r}
gismaster3 = na.omit(gismaster3)
```

we have obtained the spreadsheet we want, so now we export and we are done
```{r}
write.xlsx(gismaster3, "citystate4maplayerX.xlsx")
getwd()
```
